blocks.text:
After breakfast, a private transfer with a driver will pick you up from your hotel in Rio. The journey to Búzios takes about 3 hours.

Búzios is about 177 km north of Rio de Janeiro. The resort grew from a fishing village and is known for its beaches, coves, coastal cliffs and viewpoints.

After checking in, the rest of the day is free. You can explore the town, spend time on the beach or choose a boat trip. Búzios has a dry, moderate climate, with average maximum temperatures of around 30 degrees and minimum temperatures of around 20. Its beaches vary in their waves and wind, so over several days you can alternate between more active stretches of coast and calmer coves.

Diving, surfing, water skiing, kayaking and buggy trips are available in Búzios. Sightseeing boats offer views of the coast, with stops for swimming and snorkelling.

After sunset, life moves to the main pedestrian street, with its restaurants, bars and shops. Viewpoints overlook the ocean, wooded hills and coastal cliffs. Boat trips run along the entire coast, stopping out at sea so passengers can swim and discover the underwater world.

blocks.text:
Choose different beaches to suit the weather and your plans. The eastern, Atlantic coast is windier and suitable for sports. On the western side, the water is calmer and warmer, making these beaches better for swimming and relaxing.

Diving, trekking and boat trips can be arranged on request. Surfing, water skiing, kayaks and buggy hire for exploring the beaches and town are also available at the resort. Schooners offer trips lasting 2 or 4 hours. These may include lunch, soft drinks and caipirinhas on board, as well as stops for snorkelling.
